settings.heading: What is the difference between saliva and urine drug tests?
settings.text: Saliva tests detect recent use (typically within 24–48 hours) and allow observed collection, making them practical for on-site workplace screening. Urine tests offer a wider detection window (days to weeks depending on the substance) and broader panel options, making them suited to compliance programs and laboratory confirmation.

settings.heading: Are Andatech drug test kits compliant with Australian Standards?
settings.text: Andatech's drug test kit range includes products verified to AS/NZS 4760:2019 (oral fluid) and AS/NZS 4308:2023 (urine). Confirm the applicable standard and version on the individual product page before purchase.

settings.heading: How many drugs can a test kit detect?
settings.text: Panel count varies by product. Saliva kits in the range detect up to 8 drugs plus alcohol. Urine cups detect up to 15 drugs plus alcohol. Choose the panel count your workplace policy or industry standard requires.

settings.heading: Do I need a drug test analyser?
settings.text: An analyser is not required for a valid screening, but it removes subjective line-reading, digitises the result and creates an automatic audit record. If your process needs defensible evidence or multi-site reporting, an analyser is worth evaluating.

settings.heading: What if we need more than test kits?
settings.text: If you also need operator training, policy development, reporting or a fully managed program, start with an Andatech solutions specialist rather than choosing a product in isolation.
